source.title: Evaluating of Machine Unlearning: Robustness Verification Without Prior Modifications
source.authors: Heng Xu; Tian-Qing Zhu; Wan-Lei Zhou

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some results are conveyed only in figures.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses sample reconstruction to test whether unlearning leaves training information recoverable. Its results challenge relabel-based fine-tuning as an effective unlearning method, but the experiments use image classifiers and do not test the specified LLM attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for reconstruction after retraining-based sample- and class-level unlearning, and after relabel-based fine-tuning. These bear on residual training information, but do not test any listed version as phrased. The paper also compares verification schemes; cited results from prior work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a reconstruction-based scheme for verifying unlearning in small image classifiers (MNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR-10, SVHN). It neither tests nor relies on the LLM unlearning claim or its originals, which it does not cite. Its closest result is that random-label fine-tuning leaves recoverable training samples on MNIST. That bears on residual information after unlearning, but in a different kind of system (image classifiers, not LLMs). It also uses no recovery attack of the kinds in B–E, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of C. The reader's 'tests / T5' guess is not supported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that UnlearnGuard verifies sample- and class-level unlearning without prior modifications and stays robust to pruning and fine-tuning. They also say relabel fine-tuning does not fully remove, 'but rather amplify', the influence of targeted samples, contrary to prior work.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates sample reconstruction as a verification method, retraining from scratch as an unlearning procedure, and random-label fine-tuning as another unlearning procedure. It does not reproduce the cited LLM unlearning methods or test the listed recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The study evaluates different datasets and sample-level versus class-level requests. It reports that relabel-based fine-tuning increases the number of recovered samples.

fits_no_version.finding: After random-label relabel fine-tuning on MNIST, reconstructed samples still match training samples of the forgotten class with high SSIM. The number of recoverable samples increases after fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small image classifiers, fine-tuning-based (random-relabel) unlearning leaves training-sample information recoverable from the weights by KKT-based reconstruction, so it removes less than output metrics suggest.

fits_no_version.finding: After retraining from scratch, reconstruction SSIM drops for forgotten samples and classes but stays high for retained ones, across four image datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-based sample reconstruction can distinguish exact unlearning from retained data in small image classifiers.

record.problems: The experiments use image datasets and do not establish results for LLM unlearning. Model names and sizes are not stated. Several numerical results are presented only in figures, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. SSIM-based sample recovery is an indirect measure of knowledge recovery.

untested.parts: No LLM unlearning method, no targeted-knowledge accuracy versus chance, no general-ability check, no attack-based recovery.
No relearning attack on an unlearned model. Relabel fine-tuning is tested as the unlearning method itself, on an MNIST classifier.
No activation-direction ablation. The 'information retained' analysis is on image classifiers, not LLMs.
No robust unlearning counter-method. UnlearnGuard is a verification scheme.

record.verdict_notes: Image-classifier verification paper with no LLM content. The relabel fine-tuning result has no reported numbers beyond figures, and there are no uncertainty estimates. The unlearning in the main experiments is exact retraining, so those results say nothing about approximate-method shallowness.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test LLM unlearning at near-chance targeted accuracy while preserving general ability, or whether the listed simple attacks recover knowledge.
Relabel-based fine-tuning is tested as an unlearning method, not as an attack that fine-tunes an already-unlearned model to restore knowledge.
No activation-direction ablation is tested, and the paper does not test whether an LLM method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language change, or in-context recovery is tested.
The proposed method is for verifying unlearning, not a counter-method that resists the listed attacks.
